prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production game sprite for a top-down 2D space game; art direction Salvage Print.
Primary request: A compact north-facing industrial salvage tug/barge, squared blunt nose at top, paired chunky side pods, dark central cargo spine, broad bone armor plates with a single burnt-orange band and tiny mint cockpit. Two rear exhausts pointing down. Readable 32 pixel silhouette.
Style/medium: Rugged industrial science fiction interpreted as a sharp limited-palette woodcut pixel illustration. Broad angular armor plates, coarse carved hatching organized in intentional clusters, charcoal-black and bone-cream with oxidized burnt orange and small mint signal lights. Strong silhouettes, three-tone chiaroscuro, imperfect utilitarian asymmetry. NOT smooth rendering, not generic detailed metallic sci-fi.
Composition/framing: Deliver the actual six-frame animation sprite STRIP: 1536x256 transparent PNG, exactly six equal 256x256 cells in ONE horizontal row, with NO gutters. Each cell contains the IDENTICAL north-facing ship at exactly the same position and scale, only rear exhaust flicker changes in a smooth loop. Ship hull spans about 160x160 pixels centered in each cell, exhaust stays within central 180x180. Frames animate ONLY exhaust length/color: short, medium, long, medium, short, medium. Keep geometry, camera and hull absolutely identical. Each cell will be mechanically reduced to 48x48 for the final 288x48 barge6frame.png. Design in broad pixels so its approximately 32x32 hull reads at final resolution. No cell borders.
Lighting: consistent upper-left illumination; restrained hard banded shading. Pixel-art contour precision.
Scene/backdrop: genuine transparent alpha background, empty space fully transparent including station openings. No starfield, no shadow cast onto a backdrop.
Constraints: no labels, typography, logos, watermark, legend, scale ruler, decorative framing, UI markers, concept art layout or mockup. These are the final asset pixels. No baked docking beacon overlays on planet. No antialias softness.
